name: Balanced 4-3-3 DM Wide

slots.why: Keeps the goalkeeper's job simple and avoids requiring sweeper-keeper distribution or decision-making.
Supports the left side and can overlap when space appears without being asked to provide all of the width.

Defends simply in the central pair. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the keeper kicks long to the flanks and the midfield, not the centre-backs, links the play. Only one centre-back may use Cover.

Defends simply in the central pair, on the right. Cover is the alternate, as is the No-Nonsense Centre-Back (Defend or Cover), who clears rather than passes: the keeper kicks long to the flanks and the midfield, not the centre-backs, links the play. Only one centre-back may use Cover.
Supports the right winger and offers a safe outlet without needing to play as an aggressive wing-back.
Holds position in front of the centre-backs, breaks up attacks and gives the two central midfielders freedom to support play.
Provides a reliable link between defence and attack. A box-to-box midfielder is an alternative when the player has the legs for it.
Adds a runner from midfield so the lone striker is not left isolated and the team gets an extra body into the box.
Cuts inside to become a second goal threat and attacks the space around the lone striker.
Stays wider, carries the ball forward and supplies crosses, giving the attack width and balancing the inside forward.
Runs beyond the defence and gives the side a clear vertical outlet. Poacher is the alternative for a strong finisher with less all-round movement.

description: A simple lower-league 4-3-3 with a dedicated holding midfielder, natural width on one side and two additional runners supporting a mobile striker.
whyGood: It gives strong defensive structure and three central midfielders without requiring sophisticated build-up play. The asymmetrical front three creates both width and additional goal threat.
whyThisShape: The defensive midfielder protects the centre-backs, the two central midfielders provide one link player and one forward runner, and the front three give an immediate outlet on regains. Fairly wide spacing preserves room for the inside forward and attacking central midfielder, while slightly more direct passing and quick distribution toward the flanks move the ball forward without requiring sophisticated short build-up. Regroup restores the 4-1-4-1 defensive shape and standard pressing avoids requesting repeated challenges. Low crosses and greater discipline are starting fallbacks to review against the selected players: they suit the movement of the advanced forward, inside forward and attacking midfielder while keeping the overall structure simple.
whenToUse: As a stable lower-league default when you have one good striker, a dependable holding midfielder and usable wide attackers. It is especially useful when a 4-4-2 is being outnumbered in central midfield.
whenNotToUse: When you lack a credible lone striker or wide attackers who can threaten the defence. It can also become blunt against a very deep opponent if the inside forward and attacking central midfielder do not provide enough secondary goal threat.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Reach the forward outlets earlier without turning every possession into a long ball.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Recover the defensive shape after losing possession; this is a positioning choice, not a measured guarantee about stamina or defensive success.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute Quickly: Starts counters before the opposition can recover its defensive shape.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Flanks: Uses the natural wide outlets rather than asking the goalkeeper to force play through central pressure.
instructionRationale.Be More Disciplined: Ask players to retain the defined structure rather than adding further improvisation.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Take Long Kicks: Use the selected forward or wide outlets without demanding short build-up under pressure.

keyRequirements: A disciplined holding midfielder who protects the centre and keeps the structure intact
One reliable linking central midfielder and one genuine forward runner from midfield
An inside forward who supplies secondary goal threat
A wide player capable of preserving width and delivering from the opposite side
A mobile lone striker who threatens the space behind
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
